facts.summary: EPA announced cleanup complete on 5.3 acres of the NASA Marshall Space Flight Center portion of the USARMY/NASA Redstone Arsenal Superfund site and the release says that portion was deleted from the National Priorities List.
facts.reference: EPA news release, Huntsville, Ala., March 6, 2025
facts.quote: Cleanup has been completed for 5.3 acres of the NASA Marshall Space Flight Center portion of the site

facts.summary: Army and environmental experts held the inaugural meeting of an Environmental Restoration Leaders Working Group at Redstone Arsenal to coordinate and map out the installation's cleanup process (Army article published March 13, 2026).
facts.authority: U.S. Army Garrison Redstone Arsenal / Army public affairs
facts.quote: The primary purpose of the Environmental Restoration Leaders Working Group is to bring together key leaders

gaps: Federal installation land is generally not carried on county assessor or deed rolls; no county parcel, deed or tax record was checked for this federal site. That expectation is from general knowledge and was not verified against a Madison County source.
Army real property and garrison land records (GSA federal real property inventory, RSA Garrison real property office) were not checked.

facts.quote: The EPA is currently addressing residential soil contamination in three North Birmingham, Alabama neighborhoods.

facts.summary: WBRC reported that North Birmingham neighbors described living in the Superfund site and that one resident asked the city to buy out and relocate properties; a city spokesperson said the city continues to work with EPA on residents' concerns.
